finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls the async authorize() without await. The 403 rejection is never observed, so db.reports.remove() runs whether or not the user has the 'delete' grant. Any caller can delete any report by ID. Unauthenticated callers are probably covered too: authorize(undefined, ...) fails on user.id, but that rejection is also dropped. The dropped rejection can additionally trigger an unhandledRejection, which crashes Node 15+ by default and gives a DoS.
finding.source: Any HTTP client sends DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary :id. No grant is required.

trace.note: authorize() returns a Promise that is not awaited or checked
grants lookup is async, so the check only runs after the handler has already continued
the 403 error is thrown inside the dropped promise and never reaches the handler or Express
remove() executes unconditionally and the handler responds 204

finding.guards_checked: Checked for the await in the handler (missing). Checked for a global auth middleware (the one at lines 4-7 only copies req.session.user and does not enforce anything). Checked for any other ownership check (none). Compare PUT at line 27, which does await authorize.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: the middleware at server.js:4-7 only copies req.session.user, and authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws on failure, but the call at server.js:20 has no await, so the rejection is dropped
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so the 403 thrown at server.js:14 (or the TypeError at :10 for a missing user) becomes an unobserved rejection and db.reports.remove() at server.js:21 runs for any caller, unlike the awaited call at :27.

finding.claim: Mass assignment. PUT /reports/:id passes the whole request body to db.reports.update() with no field allowlist. A user with 'write' on a report can overwrite protected fields such as owner, id, or tenant, or any other fields on the record. Impact depends on the db layer, which is not in this codebase.
finding.source: JSON body of PUT /reports/:id, from a user who holds the 'write' grant

trace.note: express.json() parses the body into an arbitrary object
authorization checks only the 'write' action on the report, not which fields are changed
unfiltered req.body is passed to update()

finding.guards_checked: Checked for schema validation or field allowlisting (none). Checked for a db.js or model layer that could filter fields (not present in the repo, so this cannot be confirmed).

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:27 is properly awaited and throws 403 without 'write' grant, but there is no field allowlist or schema validation; db layer is absent from the repo.
verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes unfiltered req.body to db.reports.update() (the trace is accurate and the attacker is a low-privilege user with 'write' grant), but whether protected fields like owner/id/tenant can actually be overwritten depends on the db layer, which is not in this repo.
